title: Random Freezing Issues in RPG Maker MV (Performance Problem)

posts.author: Luciien
posts.body:
Hello everyone,​
I'm developing a game with RPG Maker MV, and as the game progresses, I've started experiencing
occasional small freezes
during gameplay. Here's what I've tried so far:
I enlarged the map
, but only to a necessary size.
I reduced parallel events
as much as possible.
I'm using 19 different plugins
, all of which are essential for my game’s mechanics.
I suspect the freezes might be caused by some of the plugins, but I can't figure out which ones are causing the problem. Reducing the number of plugins isn't an option because all of them are useful for my game.
My questions:
How can I determine if plugins are conflicting or causing performance issues?
I've reduced parallel events, but there are still many events (non-parallel). Can these also affect performance?
Is there a better and practical way to improve performance?
I’d appreciate any advice or suggestions. Thanks in advance!

posts.author: SGHarlekin

Likely has to do with the default coding of pixi's garbage collection.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
It's not the number of parallel processes that count, but their quality.
One badly designed parallel process event can cause more lag than a hundred correctly designed ones.
Basically each parallel process needs the correct number of waitframes - the wait command basically tells the engine "skip this event for x frames" - which causes a pause in an action button event, but reduces processing and lag in a parallel process.
unfortunately the correct number is different depending on the other PP in the game - not enough and it still creates lag, too much and the game's reaction (instead of processing) is slowed.
Luciien said:
How can I determine if plugins are conflicting
Click to expand...
Basically only by experience.
So the best way is to post a screenshot of your plugin manager and allow the community with their greater experience to check if there is anything wrong.
There are a lot of quirks in plug-ins that are known to us, but rarely are known by new users who never read much here.
For example, with yanfly's plug-ins their order is extremely critical - have more than a few in the wrong order and they will have extremely strange results.
Luciien said:
many events (non-parallel). Can these also affect performance?
Click to expand...
not in any detectable measure, not on modern computers.
ten, twenty years ago that was different, but even then you needed multiple hundreds of events on a single map before it became detectable.

posts.author: utunnels
posts.body:
The game should be able to handle a few dozens of events without slow down. Parallel events don't slow down the game directly. Unless they do something stressful to your computer.
I can only guess:
1) Plugins that add display elements, like HUD, but I don't think it is map size related.
2) Event indicator (labels over their heads), but I think I need to actually read the code to judge. Usually they don't refresh every frame considering the author is not a novice. Shadows are the same I think.
3) There are actually more events than it is shown in your screenshot. For example you use event spawner to spawn a few hundreds events.
4) Your pc is too old, have a faulty display driver, etc. Maybe you can make a smaller demo so different people can test if they have the same problem on their hardwares.
